title: ATKINSON, James. AN ACCOUNT OF THE STATE OF AGRICULTURE & GRAZING IN NEW SOUTH WALES; including observations on the soil
description: ATKINSON, James. AN ACCOUNT OF THE STATE OF AGRICULTURE & GRAZING IN NEW SOUTH WALES; including observations on the soils and general appearance of the country, and some of its most useful natural productions; with an account of the various methods of clearing and improving lands, breeding and grazing live stock, erecting buildings, the System of Employing Convicts, and the expense of Labour generally; the mode of applying for grants of land; with other information important to those who are about to emigrate to that Country; the result of several years’ residence and practical experience in those matters in the colony. Octavo, with half-title, terminal advertisement leaf, and errata slip, with the large folding coloured aquatint view of Port Jackson and Sydney (expertly laid down), three coloured aquatint plates and one plan, and folding handcoloured map of New South Wales by Joseph Cross (expertly laid down), the map with two inset maps, and eleven engraved views and pictorial title, four early leaves including title strengthened at gutter, uncut in later boards retaining the original printed and decorated front and back panels; the copy of Ivo Hammet with his characteristic monogram on the back endpaper. London, Cross, 1826. First edition: the very scarce first book on Australian agriculture. James Atkinson, a farmer from a farming family, served as a clerk in the naval service during the Napoleonic wars. Having become, like many others, an economic casualty of the peace, Atkinson determined to emigrate and raised enough capital to obtain a land grant in New South Wales, establishing his property in the Bong Bong district in 1821. While in England in 1824, Atkinson was assailed “with innumerable questions and enquiries respecting the present state of New South Wales, and especially of its Agriculture and Grazing”. This determined him to write an account of the pastoral and agricultural frontier in New South Wales, based on his extensive personal experience. His survey of the agricultural districts and the larger pastoral properties was also a very practical handbook of “rural and domestic economy”, which seems to have been of real assistance to the settlers with capital who had begun to arrive at Sydney through the early 1820s, as post-war prospects in Britain showed no signs of improving. Having lived an obscure life in England, Atkinson left a significant heritage in New South Wales. He published two further works, on sheep farming and on brewing, and was active in civic affairs. Unassuming, intelligent, and humane, Atkinson married late, in 1827, to one of the colony’s more remarkable women, Charlotte Waring, tutor to the children of Hannibal Macarthur. Before Atkinson’s early death in 1834, he and Charlotte had four children. His youngest was the future novelist, Louisa Atkinson; his wife, Charlotte, wrote the first Australian book for children, published in 1841. When first published in 1826, the book was issued in two forms: “Price Seven Shillings, or, including a large Map and View of Sydney, Fourteen Shillings”. The present lot is the very rare issue including both the view and the map. Abbey, 572; Ferguson, 1054; Richards, 126; Wantrup, 279. Estimate $10,000/15,000

title: BAUDIN. PÉRON, François Auguste, Louis Claude de Saulces de Freycinet, Charles Lesueur, and Nicholas Petit.
description: BAUDIN. PÉRON, François Auguste, Louis Claude de Saulces de Freycinet, Charles Lesueur, and Nicholas Petit. VOYAGE DE DÉCOUVERTES AUX TERRES AUSTRALES, fait par ordre du Gouvernement, sur les corvettes le Géographe, le Naturaliste, et la goèlette le Casuarina, pendant les années 1800, 1801,1802,1803 et 1804; Historique. Redigé par Péron, Et continué par M. Louis de Freycinet. Seconde Édition, Revue, Corrigée et Augmentée par M. Louis de Freycinet, Capitaine de vaisseau, chevalier de S.-Louis et de la Légion-d’Honneur, correspondant de l’Academie royale des sciences de l’Institut de France, et membre de plusiers autres sociétés savantes; commandant du Casuarina pendant l’expedition. Ouvrage enrichi d’un superbe atlas composé de 68 planches, dont 27 coloriées. Tome Premier. [- Quatrième.] Four octavo volumes of text, and a quarto atlas with 68 plates (many handcoloured, three double page, scattered pale foxing), one text leaf worn, bound in half calf and marbled boards and endpapers of the period, Atlas joint splitting. Paris, Arthus Bertrand, 1824. The extremely scarce and importantly revised second edition of the official Péron-Freycinet account of the Baudin voyage to the Pacific. In the first edition of the official Péron-Freycinet account published between 1807 and 1816, Péron and Freycinet failed to acknowledge the discoveries of Flinders, Grant, or Murray on the south coast, taking all the credit to themselves. Notably they renamed the south coast “Terre Napoléon”, supplying most of the features on the coast named by Flinders with French names. The publication of Flinders’s own account of the Investigator voyage in 1814 did much to discredit the pretensions and deceptions of the French. “This very scarce second edition was prepared by Freycinet after he returned from his own expedition to the Pacific between 1817 and 1820. It is not generally known that the 1824 second edition of the “Partie Historique” contains some significant changes and additions to the first edition. The maps and charts of the first edition atlas, which bore the nationalistic and ambitious name of Terre Napoléon and included imperial French names for many parts of the coast, were omitted or greatly altered for the second edition atlas; the atlas notably includes twenty-five plates new to this edition, many of which are coloured. “Reflecting the political reality of the times, Freycinet also made substantial changes to the maps and charts in the second edition atlas, replacing not only the nationalistic and ambitious name of Terre Napoléon but also the imperial French names given to many parts of the coast, finally recognising the just claims of the British navigators, in particular Matthew Flinders, to the discovery of the Australian coast. Copies of the second edition of the “Partie historique” are noticeably rarer, copy for copy, than the first edition and are prized accordingly” (Wantrup). Ferguson, 978 and 979; Wantrup, 82. Estimate $10,000/15,000

title: COLLINS, David. AN ACCOUNT OF THE ENGLISH COLONY IN NEW SOUTH WALES, from its first Settlement, in January 1788, to Augu
description: COLLINS, David. AN ACCOUNT OF THE ENGLISH COLONY IN NEW SOUTH WALES, from its first Settlement, in January 1788, to August 1801: with Remarks on the Dispositions, Customs, Manners, &c. of the Native Inhabitants of that Country... The Second edition. Quarto, with a map and folding chart, 24 engraved plates (three handcoloured), eight engravings in the text (two handcoloured), without the half-title, a lovely copy in contemporary full Russia gilt, expertly rebacked, corners bruised. London, T. Cadell and W. Davies, 1804. Second edition: the preferred issue with the natural history plates handcoloured. Collins’s income had been severely affected by his long service in New South Wales and it was largely in an attempt to eke out the family income that he had published his two-volume history of the colony in 1798 – 1802. He began the work of abridging these two volumes late in 1802, intending to issue a cheaper edition so as to reach new readers who could not afford the expensive two-volume edition. When he was appointed Lieutenant-Governor of the intended new settlement at Port Phillip, the whole job of editing fell to his wife, Maria. She continued her husband’s revision quickly and skilfully, and completed the book with new information available to the end of 1803. Davidson, pp. 91-2; Ferguson, 390; Wantrup, 21. title: DIXON, James. NARRATIVE OF A VOYAGE TO NEW SOUTH WALES, AND VAN DIEMAN’S LAND, in the Ship Skelton, during the year 1820
description: DIXON, James. NARRATIVE OF A VOYAGE TO NEW SOUTH WALES, AND VAN DIEMAN’S LAND, in the Ship Skelton, during the year 1820. With observations on the state of these colonies, and a variety of information, calculated to be useful to emigrants. By James Dixon, Commander of the Skelton. With an appendix, containing Governor M’Quarie’s Report regarding Van Dieman’s Land, Tables of the Population, List of Articles Suitable for Exportation, &c. &c. Duodecimo, complete with half-title and the rare frontispiece, without the advertisement leaves found in some copies, uncut in later half calf, the copy of Frank Hobill Cole with bookplate. Edinburgh and London, John Anderson, Jun. and Longman, Hurst, Rees, Orme, and Browne, 1822. A notable rarity: complete with the frontispiece silhouette portrait of Cobawn Wogy that is frequently missing. One of the key books documenting the colonies under Governor Lachlan Macquarie, this rare emigrant’s guide to Van Diemen’s Land and New South Wales was written by the captain of the ship Skelton, who visited New South Wales and Van Diemen’s Land in 1820. Dixon published this narrative on his return. The long appendix contains Macquarie’s report on Van Diemen’s Land. The rarely found frontispiece is based on a caricature of Cobawn Wogy, an Aboriginal ‘chief’ of Ashe Island, Hunter’s River, in New South Wales, painted by the convict artist Richard Browne. Ferguson, 858; Wantrup, 57. Estimate $8000/12,000

description: LEICHHARDT, Ludwig. JOURNAL OF AN OVERLAND EXPEDITION IN AUSTRALIA, from Moreton Bay to Port Essington, a distance of upwards of 3000 miles, during the years 1844-5. title: [OXFORD, Edward.] LIGHTS AND SHADOWS OF MELBOURNE LIFE by John Freeman.
description: [OXFORD, Edward.] LIGHTS AND SHADOWS OF MELBOURNE LIFE by John Freeman. Octavo, a fine copy in an attractive author’s presentation binding of red morocco, spine fully gilt, gilt inner dentelles, all edges gilt, marbled endpapers, narrow strip of dressing on the back board restored, with the bookplate of Douglas Lord Loch. London, Sampson Low, 1888. Very scarce: a specially-bound author’s presentation copy, inscribed to the Governor of Victoria, Sir Henry Loch, of the first and only edition of this collection of essays in the Mayhew tradition, describing the variety of Melbourne life. Oxford attempted to assassinate the Queen in 1840. Found guilty but insane, he spent 27 years in English asylums. Released in 1867 but exiled for life, he came to Melbourne where he married, living in Albert Park in the 1880s and 1890s. Oxford’s identity with his touchingly ambiguous Australian persona, ‘John Freeman’, has only recently been established: ‘Freeman’ himself wrote to G.H. Haydon in 1889 “Even my wife, the sharer of my joys and sorrows, is no wiser than the rest of the world”. This is an extraordinarily poignant copy, inscribed by an attempted regicide to that monarch’s representative “with the author’s loyal respects”. Ferguson, 9768. Estimate $400/600

title: STOKES, John Lort. DISCOVERIES IN AUSTRALIA; with an account of the Coasts and Rivers explored and surveyed during the V
description: STOKES, John Lort. DISCOVERIES IN AUSTRALIA; with an account of the Coasts and Rivers explored and surveyed during the Voyage of H.M.S. Beagle, In the Years 1837 – 38 – 39 – 40 – 41 – 42 – 43. By Command of the Lords Commissioners of the Admiralty. Also a Narrative of Captain Owen Stanley’s Visits to the Islands in the Arafura Sea. Two volumes, octavo, with 26 plates and eight folding charts (six loosely enclosed), repaired original cloth, with bookplate of James B. Walker. London, Boone, 1846. First edition. In 1837 John Clements Wickham was sent to survey and complete the discovery of those parts of the northern coast of Australia not already charted by Flinders or King and still known only from the rough charts of Louis de Freycinet. Wickham was also instructed to improve the charts of key areas of the coast such as Torres Strait, Bass Strait and the approaches to the new and developing settlements at Adelaide and Swan River, and to search for any large rivers on the north-west coast which, it was hoped, would open up the northern coast and the interior to exploration and further settlement – as part of this larger plan the Beagle transported George Grey’s land party to the north-west coast in 1837. In 1841, when Wickham was relieved due to ill-health, Lieutenant Stokes was placed in command. In the course of this expedition Wickham and Stokes completed the discovery of the north-west coast and accurately charted for the first time other stretches of coast. On the northern coast they discovered and partly explored five rivers, while Stokes and his men also undertook many expeditions inland which are recorded in this official account. Ferguson, 4406; Wantrup, 89. Estimate $3000/5000

title: TENCH, Watkin. VOYAGE À LA BAIE BOTANIQUE; Avec une Description du nouveau Pays de Galles Méridional, de ses habitans, de ses productions, &c.
description: TENCH, Watkin. VOYAGE À LA BAIE BOTANIQUE; Avec une Description du nouveau Pays de Galles Méridional, de ses habitans, de ses productions, &c. &c. quelques détails relatifs à M. de la Peyrouse, pendant son séjour à la Baie Botanique... A laquelle on a ajouté le récit historique de la Découverte de la nouvelle Hollande, & des différens Voyages qui y ont été faits par les Européens. Octavo, with folding map (at page 262), with the half-title, early calf, modern rebacking, Nancye Kent Perry copy with bookplate. Paris, Letellier, 1789. One of two French editions in 1789 (no priority established). The present edition is printed in larger type and is substantially longer, with an 86-page appendix entitled “Récit historique de la découverte de la Nouvelle Hollande et du nouveau Pays de Galles Méridional”. This copy includes the rare folding map, “Carte de la Baye Botanique et des Havres Adjacens sur la Côte du Nouveau Pays de Galles Méridional”, not listed in the table of contents and lacking in most copies. Ferguson, 53. Estimate $200/400

title: TENCH, Captain Watkin, and George PATTERSON. VOYAGES DANS LE PAYS DES HOTTENTOTS… à la Baye Botanique, et dans la Nouvelle Hollande.
description: TENCH, Captain Watkin, and George PATTERSON. VOYAGES DANS LE PAYS DES HOTTENTOTS… à la Baye Botanique, et dans la Nouvelle Hollande. Traduits de l’Anglois, accompagnés de détails précieux relatifs à M. de la Pérouse. Octavo, some paper restoration to leaves, modern quarter French burgundy morocco, new endpapers. Paris, Letellier, 1790. Second (revised and enlarged) Letellier edition of Tench’s eye-witness account of Australia’s settlement – along with the account of La Pérouse at Botany Bay, together with Patterson’s narrative of travels in South Africa. Ferguson, 96. Estimate $200/400

title: TENCH, Watkin. A COMPLETE ACCOUNT OF THE SETTLEMENT AT PORT JACKSON, in New South Wales, including an accurate descripti
description: TENCH, Watkin. A COMPLETE ACCOUNT OF THE SETTLEMENT AT PORT JACKSON, in New South Wales, including an accurate description of the Situation of the Colony; of the Natives; and of its natural productions: Taken on the spot... Quarto, with folding “Map of the hitherto unexplored country contiguous to Port Jackson…”, uncut in the original boards, sympathetically rebacked, new spine label. London, G. Nicol and J. Sewell, 1793. First edition: in nice original condition. Captain Watkin Tench was the only First Fleet chronicler to publish more than one book. He had returned to England with other marines in the Gorgon in 1792 and his very scarce second account of the colony was published over a year later, at the end of 1793. Tench “completes his account of the first years of the colony and brings his record of events down to the end of the first four years of settlement. The map and text give important and full details of the early expeditions of discovery to the south and to the west, including those which Tench led himself. As an accurate, well-written and acutely observed account of the earliest years of Australia’s colonisation, it is a most important addition to any collection of Australian books. It is rare despite the hundreds of copies that were originally printed…” (Wantrup). Davidson, p. 76; Ferguson, 171; Wantrup, 16. Estimate $8000/12,000

title: WARBURTON, Colonel Peter Egerton.
description: WARBURTON, Colonel Peter Egerton. JOURNEY ACROSS THE WESTERN INTERIOR OF AUSTRALIA… With an Introduction and Additions by Charles H. Eden, Esq. Author of “My Wife and I in Queensland.” Edited by H. W. Bates, Esq. Assistant Secretary of the Royal Geographical Society. With Illustrations and a Map. Octavo, with half-title and advertisements, frontispiece portrait and eight other plates, and a large folding map, original green cloth over bevelled boards, decorated in gilt and black. London, Sampson Low, Marston, Low, & Searle, 1875. First edition of the formal narrative of Warburton’s last, great expedition of 1873-1874 from the Telegraph Line to the west coast which won the race to cross the continent from east to west. The Warburton, Forrest, and Giles expeditions are pre-eminent in the history of exploration in the 1870s and this London account of Warburton’s victorious expedition is an essential document in the story. Ferguson, 18187; Wantrup, 201. Estimate $500/800

title: WILLS, William John. A SUCCESSFUL EXPLORATION THROUGH THE INTERIOR OF AUSTRALIA, From Melbourne to the Gulf of Carpentaria.
description: WILLS, William John. A SUCCESSFUL EXPLORATION THROUGH THE INTERIOR OF AUSTRALIA, From Melbourne to the Gulf of Carpentaria. From the Journals and Letters of William John Wills. Edited by his father, William Wills. Octavo, with half-title and inserted advertisements, engraved frontispiece with pale foxing, engraved portrait of Wills, and a folding map (old paper strengthening on verso), bound in modern half calf with new endpapers. London, Richard Bentley, 1863. First edition of what might, by default, be considered the ‘official’ account of the expedition, edited from his letters and journals by Wills’s father. “The largest, the most expensive and the worst led expedition yet seen in Australia, the Victorian Exploring Expedition became a symbol of intercolonial rivalry. There can be little doubt that the prime objective of the expedition when it set out in August 1860 was to beat Stuart’s South Australian expedition to the north coast at any cost... Bentley’s edition of Wills’s journals is the most extensive contemporary account of the expedition and must be considered essential to a collection...” (Wantrup). Ferguson, 18622; Maria, 192; Wantrup, 172. Estimate $500/800 Lot 38 (part) Australian Topographical Art and Illustration (lots 38 – 55)

title: SCOTT, Henry Montagu Douglas, (later Lord Montagu of Beaulieu).
description: SCOTT, Henry Montagu Douglas, (later Lord Montagu of Beaulieu). SUITE OF FOUR ORIGINAL WATERCOLOURS, Brisbane and Sydney. Four original sketches of Australian scenes, watercolour and pencil, each approximately 103 x 173 mm., on paper, titled in ink, separately mounted, framed and (in three cases) glazed. Comprising: “Kangaroo Point July 11th 1853 Brisbane”; “View of the Bay from One Tree Hill July 1853”; “Brisbane & River from ranges at the back July 1853” (in ink) also titled “Brisbane & River from ranges of One Tree Hill July 1863” (in pencil); and “Botany Bay, Sept. 185-”. Accomplished British amateur watercolourist and politician Lord Henry John Douglas-Scott-Montagu (born 1832), also known as Lord Henry Scott, Baron Montagu of Beaulieu, Lord Henry Montagu-Douglas-Scott, was the second son of the Duke of Buccleuch. He was a naturally skilled artist and studied drawing and painting at Eton. For reasons of health, Lord Henry travelled overseas in the English winters from his mid-teens with his tutor, Henry Stobart. In 1853 they embarked for South Africa, Australasia, the South Pacific, and India. The party landed at Sydney in March 1853 and they enjoyed the hospitality of the colonial great and the good in Sydney, Newcastle, and Brisbane. Lord Henry painted watercolours in his sketchbook of the many places they visited. In an earlier visit to Sydney, he had taken lessons from Conrad Martens and owned several of his paintings, including “View of Brisbane from Kangaroo Point” (now National Library of Australia) as something of a foil to his own “Kangaroo Point, Brisbane”. Lord Henry only painted for his own pleasure, for friends and relations. His paintings and drawings were never exhibited or sold. Examples of his work are found in the National Library of Australia, the John Oxley Library, and the Mitchell Library. See further Design and Art Australia Online. Estimate $3000/5000 Lot 38 (part) Lot 39

title: LYCETT, Joseph. VIEWS IN AUSTRALIA OR NEW SOUTH WALES, & VAN DIEMEN’S LAND Delineated, in Fifty Views, with descriptive
description: LYCETT, Joseph. VIEWS IN AUSTRALIA OR NEW SOUTH WALES, & VAN DIEMEN’S LAND Delineated, in Fifty Views, with descriptive Letter Press, Dedicated by Permission, to The Right Honble. Earl Bathurst, &c. &c. &c. By J. Lycett, Artist to Major General Macquarie, late Governor of those Colonies. Oblong folio, handcoloured lithographed title and 48 handcoloured aquatint views after drawings by Joseph Lycett (plates slightly browned and a few creased), with descriptive text (some with neat paper repairs, including to one full-page tear), folding engraved map of Van Diemen’s Land, and folding engraved map of New South Wales supplied from another work, bound in more recent half morocco, with (the notable) bookplate of Bernard Gore Brett. London, J. Souter, 1825. First edition of the finest Australian topographical plate book and the outstanding artistic monument to the age of Macquarie. Joseph Lycett, a forger and professional painter of portraits and miniatures, arrived in New South Wales in 1814 on the same ship that brought James Wallis to the colony. A little over twelve months after his arrival he was again convicted of forgery and sentenced to a term in Newcastle, the place of punishment for convicts who committed further crimes in the colony. Here he came again into contact with James Wallis, who arrived to take command of the penal settlement about a year after Lycett had been sent there. Lycett’s good work in designing the new church in Newcastle, his painted altar-piece and the other drawings and paintings he made for Wallis earned him a conditional pardon in 1819. Macquarie was clearly impressed by his skill and employed him somewhat in the capacity of unofficial government artist, finally granting him an absolute pardon in 1821. The pardon enabled him to return to England in 1823 and finish the book of views he had been planning. The 48 views in this work offer a comprehensive record of Macquarie’s Australia, from the settled areas to the frontier. In particular, Lycett’s depiction of various private mansions and country seats – demonstrating the progress of wealth and civilisation in the colonies – is an incomparable record of early colonial architecture and garden design. See Ferguson, 1031; see Wantrup, 218b. Estimate $20,000/30,000 Lot 39

title: CARMICHAEL, John. SELECT VIEWS OF SYDNEY, NEW SOUTH WALES. DRAWN AND ENGRAVED BY JOHN CARMICHAEL. Drawn and Engraved by John Carmichael.
description: CARMICHAEL, John. SELECT VIEWS OF SYDNEY, NEW SOUTH WALES. DRAWN AND ENGRAVED BY JOHN CARMICHAEL. Drawn and Engraved by John Carmichael. Quarto, pp. [iv] (engraved title-leaf with vignette, blank leaf) + [2] (dedication, dated May 1829, verso blank), [3] – 6 (letterpress descriptions) + six finely engraved plates, sewn without wrappers, a few traces of pale added colouring, careful paper restoration throughout, preserved in a bookform box. Sydney, A. Hill, 1829. First edition of this very rare series of engraved views by the colonial artist, John Carmichael, and one of a mere handful of topographical plate books produced in Australia before the gold rushes. Ferguson, 1250; Kerr, pp. 134-5; Wantrup, 223. Estimate $10,000/15,000

title: MARTENS, Conrad. SKETCHES IN THE ENVIRONS OF SYDNEY; Being part of a series of sketches intended to illustrate the scene
description: MARTENS, Conrad. SKETCHES IN THE ENVIRONS OF SYDNEY; Being part of a series of sketches intended to illustrate the scenery of New South Wales… [wrapper title]. Oblong quarto, 16 lithographed plates (of 20), loosely enclosed in the wrappers of three parts (two of these distressed), some plates hand-finished by the artist, preserved in a folding half morocco box. Sydney, Published by the Artist, 1850-1. Very rare: to eke out the limited income he earned from his painting and teaching, Martens published a set of twenty hand-finished lithographed views of Sydney and the surrounding countryside in 1850-1. These twenty views were first issued in two sets, totalling five parts. In July 1851, after the publication of the first edition had been completed, Martens issued – also in five parts – another impression of the plates as plain lithographs without the added washes and tints which he applied in the first edition. Martens was one of the foremost colonial artists of his time and played a key role in the history of Australian art and his work is properly much prized but both editions, indeed even single parts, of this splendid oblong quarto work are very rare. The present group comprises plates from both editions. See Ferguson, 5443-4; see Wantrup, 243a-b. Estimate $12,000/18,000

title: TULLOCH, David. FIRST SERIES. HAM’S FIVE VIEWS OF THE GOLD FIELDS of Mount Alexander and Ballarat, in the Colony of Vict
description: TULLOCH, David. FIRST SERIES. HAM’S FIVE VIEWS OF THE GOLD FIELDS of Mount Alexander and Ballarat, in the Colony of Victoria, Drawn on the spot by D. Tulloch, Engraved and Published by Thomas Ham. Oblong folio, letterpress title-page and five tinted lithographed plates, with leaves of letterpress description, illustrated by six vignettes of goldfields scenes by Tulloch, bound with the wrappers in later half calf, Edge-Partington copy with bookplate. Melbourne, Engraved and Published by Thomas Ham, 1852. First edition: probably the earliest colonial plate book inspired by the Victorian gold rushes. Tulloch’s views are perhaps the best known goldfields illustrations after those of Gill. In contrast to Gill’s small octavo volume of lithographed sketches published in the same year, Tulloch’s work is a large volume, the first Victorian plate book published in a large format. The tinted lithographed plates were printed in three colours and appear to be the earliest examples of three-colour printing published in Australia. Tulloch had arrived in the Port Phillip District in 1848 and was employed by Thomas Ham as an engraver, a trade he continued in for many years. These five views published in 1852 are unquestionably his best and most enduring work. Tulloch’s book is also sometimes known as “Ham’s Views” because the printed title-page gives greater prominence to the publisher than the artist. The title-page describes these five plates as the “First Series” but no further series was issued. Ferguson, 17391; Kerr, pp. 342 and 812-3; Wantrup, 253. Estimate $2600/3200

title: TERRY, Frederick C. LANDSCAPE SCENERY Illustrating Sydney, Paramatta, Richmond, Maitland, Windsor, and Port Jackson, New South Wales.
description: TERRY, Frederick C. LANDSCAPE SCENERY Illustrating Sydney, Paramatta, Richmond, Maitland, Windsor, and Port Jackson, New South Wales. Oblong quarto, with title and 38 engraved plates by F.C. Terry; in the original ornately gilt-decorated red morocco-grain cloth, “Australian Keepsake 1855” in gilt on the front board, all edges gilt, Sydney and Melbourne, Sands and Kenny, 1855 (but December, 1854). First edition of Terry’s well-known series of delicate vignette views of Sydney scenes. This is the first issue, with the errata slip dated December 23, 1854, that is present only in the earliest copies issued. John Sands, an enterprising English emigrant, was the first to recognise the potential market for popular books of Australian views. His first venture in the field was in 1854 when he commissioned a series of landscape views of Sydney and the surrounding districts from Frederick Terry and had them engraved in England for publication and sale in Australia. For some unknown reason Sands had 39 plates prepared but included only 38 of these in the published copies: the plate excluded from the present copy is – as often – the unnumbered “Double Bay, from South Head Road” (see Wantrup, loc.cit. below). In December 1854 Sands was advertising the Australian Keepsake for sale at twenty-five shillings. His next venture was to commission S.T. Gill to prepare a series of views of Victoria: Victoria Illustrated was issued in December 1856. Ferguson, 15440a (illdescribed); Wantrup, 259a and pp. 440-442 (q.v.). Estimate $600/800

title: GILL, Samuel Thomas. VICTORIA ILLUSTRATED. Oblong quarto, engraved title-page and 45 steel-engraved plates, with probabl
description: GILL, Samuel Thomas. VICTORIA ILLUSTRATED. Oblong quarto, engraved title-page and 45 steel-engraved plates, with probably later handcolouring, early quarter roan, all edges gilt. Melbourne & Sydney, Sands & Kenny, 1857 but December 1856. First edition: Gill’s celebrated, lively depictions scenes in Melbourne, Geelong, the goldfields townships, and elsewhere in the Victorian countryside. Ferguson, 15440b; Wantrup, 260a. Estimate $600/800 Lot 45

title: GILL, Samuel Thomas. PART THE FIRST CONTAINING 24 SKETCHES OF THE VICTORIA GOLD DIGGINGS AND DIGGERS AS THEY ARE By S.T.G. [wrapper title].
description: GILL, Samuel Thomas. PART THE FIRST CONTAINING 24 SKETCHES OF THE VICTORIA GOLD DIGGINGS AND DIGGERS AS THEY ARE By S.T.G. [wrapper title]. Series of 24 lithographs, each in window mount, housed in two cloth bookform boxes, leather spine labels. Melbourne, Lithographed & Published By Macartney & Galbraith, August, 1852. Rare: “drawn on the stone by Gill himself, the plates retain the freshness and wry observation which characterise his best watercolour drawings” (Wantrup). Gill’s busy views of goldfields life and early Melbourne street scenes have helped shape the way Australians see their past. Even when his work was more within the general tradition of urban and pastoral topography his characteristic emphasis on the human element in the landscape is most apparent and what one might expect to be arid sketches of city buildings, for example, are portrayed as scenes of vibrant human activity. Ferguson, 9920; Wantrup, 244. Estimate $12,000/15,000 Lot 46

title: GILL, Samuel Thomas. PART 1, PRICE 10s.
description: GILL, Samuel Thomas. PART 1, PRICE 10s. 6d. SKETCHES OF THE VICTORIA GOLD DIGGINGS AND DIGGERS AS THEY ARE. By S.T.G. [all published]. Quarto, 24 tinted lithographed plates; in the original lithographed titling-wrapper, decorated in close facsimile of the Melbourne edition with vignettes of goldfields life, with advertisements on the versos, the plain spine gone, preserved in a quarter morocco box. London, H.H. Collins & Co. and Piper Brothers & Co., 1853. Rare: the London edition of Gill’s first substantial goldfields view book published in Melbourne in 1852. The plates in this London edition are much larger than the original Melbourne plates and are printed as tinted lithographs on a cream ground. Only this first part was published in a London edition. Distinctly rare in original wrappers. Ferguson, 9920a; Wantrup, 245. Estimate $5000/7000

title: GILL, Samuel Thomas. SKETCHES IN VICTORIA DRAWN ON STONE by S.T.G. No.
description: GILL, Samuel Thomas. SKETCHES IN VICTORIA DRAWN ON STONE by S.T.G. No. 1 [– 3]... [wrapper title]. Three parts, oblong octavo, each with eight plain lithographs, sewn in the repaired original titling-wrappers to Part 1, a little soiling, preserved in an elaborate quarto custom-made bookform box. Melbourne, James J. Blundell & Co., [1855]. Very rare: Gill’s first essay in urban topography. Blundell and Gill made enterprising use of Gill’s popularity, issuing his various collections in various formats and even as illustrated letter paper. Sketches in Victoria was a major undertaking issued over 1855-6, and probably only concluded by Gill’s departure for Sydney – the fourth and final part was ‘short’, comprising only five plates instead of the eight issued in each preceding part. As publication proceeded, Blundell issued the separate parts in cumulative combinations. The present set is a cumulative issue of the first three parts (as noted by Ferguson). Sets (and individual plates) are usually seen as tinted lithographs; the present set is on the different, more absorbent, paper that is used for the rare handcoloured issues. It is possible (and we strongly suspect) that the tinted lithographs were issued later. A short fourth and final part of the Sketches, comprising five lithographs only, was published subsequently. Ferguson, 9922; Wantrup, 248 (part). Estimate $3000/5000

title: GILL, Samuel Thomas (loosely after).
description: GILL, Samuel Thomas (loosely after). Paul Jerrard & Son (printed for) Messrs. Newbold & Co. SKETCHES OF AUSTRALIAN LIFE AND SCENERY – Complete in Twelve Plates… [caption title]. Twelve handcoloured lithographs (complete), 170 x 260 mm (plate), with printed caption titles and explanatory text, one plate trimmed and mounted, two with short marginal tears sealed on verso, bound in rebacked old half calf and cloth boards (stained), leather titling label on front board, new endpapers. London, Published by Paul Jerrard & Son for the Proprietor Messrs. Newbold & Co., n.d. but 1850s. Very rare: complete series of handcoloured Australian goldfields lithographs, loosely after the illustrations of S.T. Gill. The views are: No. 1. Sunday at the Diggings; No. 2. The Lost Bushman or the Unfortunate Digger that never Returned; No. 3. A New Rush; No. 4. A Concert on a New Rush, or Gold Diggings in Australia; No. 5. Bushrangers waiting for the Mails in New South Wales; No. 6. A Corrobory, or Native Dance [this trimmed and mounted, with the descriptive text but with the series title in good pen facsimile]; No. 7. A Native Sepulchre or Aboriginal Mode of Burial; No. 8. Christmas on the Diggings…; No. 9. Our Convicts What We Do and What Becomes of Them; No. 10. The Way Her Majesty’s Mails and the Public Protectors are Served in New South Wales; No. 11. The New Chum’s Arrival on a Gold Diggings; No. 12. Prospecting for Gold or Rewarded at Last. Edge-Partington, p. 16; Ferguson, 15738b; Wantrup, 255. Estimate $6000/10,000

title: GILL, Samuel Thomas (mainly after).
description: GILL, Samuel Thomas (mainly after). ADLER, C. (printed by). [MELBOURNE ROSE]. Engraved and chromolithographed circular roseate novelty souvenir, opened approximately 260 mm (extreme diameter); with four fold lines, as issued, some foxing. Hamburg, From C. Adler’s Printing Establishment, circa 1860s. A rare Gill piracy and a very attractive novelty souvenir. Folded to form a small bouquet of pink roses printed in colour, the piece opens to form a circle with twenty-eight separate miniature engraved vignettes of (mainly) Melbourne streetscapes, buildings, etc. Most of the engravings appear to derive from Victoria Illustrated and other images by Gill. The Rose was evidently several times reprinted (as one would expect). The present example like the Davidson copy (sale in our rooms, 4-5 August 2008, lot 167) has the publisher’s imprint on both recto and verso. There were at least two other versions of this Melbourne Rose produced: one we know to have been nominated “The Melbourne Rose Part II” on a printed envelope. Estimate $800/1400

title: GILL, Samuel Thomas. THE AUSTRALIAN SKETCHBOOK. By S.T.G. Printed in Colours & Published by Hamel & Ferguson.
description: GILL, Samuel Thomas. THE AUSTRALIAN SKETCHBOOK. By S.T.G. Printed in Colours & Published by Hamel & Ferguson. Oblong folio, illustrated chromolithographed title-page (verso blank) and 24 chromolithographs, each in a window mount, preserved in a leather folding box. Melbourne, Hamel & Ferguson, [1865]. Gill’s last and most renowned work, published after Gill had returned to Melbourne in 1864, this fine album, depicting in his characteristic style the life of the settlers and Aborigines, is widely considered to be his masterpiece. The twenty-four plates display the full range of Gill’s artistic interests. There are no urban scenes in this collection but Gill’s characteristic rural themes are all represented: the goldfields, the Aborigines, scenes of drama in the bush – whether bushrangers or lost children – as well as outback scenes of a more mundane or even pathetic nature such as “Bush Funeral” and “Native Sepulchre”, all drawn with Gill’s unfailing sense of irony and his eye for detail. Unlike all Gill’s earlier plate books this final and most mature work was published in a grand oblong folio format in a style comparable to the great plate books of Nicholas Chevalier and Eugen von Guérard published in the same decade. Ferguson, 9924f; Wantrup, 251. Estimate $3000/5000

title: GILL, Samuel Thomas, F.R. Nixon, Samuel Calvert, and O. Korn.
description: GILL, Samuel Thomas, F.R. Nixon, Samuel Calvert, and O. Korn. 14 VIEWS OF OLD ADELAIDE from Sketches in 1840 – 1849 by S.T. Gill, F.R. Nixon, S. Calvert & O. Korn. Oblong octavo, tinted lithographed upper wrapper, 14 tinted lithographs, without index leaf nor subscribers, fine copy in modern calf retaining the rare pictorial stiff wrappers, gilt edges. Adelaide, E.S. Wigg & Son, no date, circa 1876. First edition: Ferguson notes, on George Robertson’s authority, that only 200 copies were printed. Ferguson, 9924e. Estimate $500/800

title: CHEVALIER, Nicholas. N. CHEVALIER’S ALBUM OF CHROMO LITHOGRAPHS [cover title].
description: CHEVALIER, Nicholas. N. CHEVALIER’S ALBUM OF CHROMO LITHOGRAPHS [cover title]. Large folio, twelve chromolithographed plates, each mounted on a stiff white sheet, one with the original small printed title label on the verso (supplied in facsimile on nine others), the plate of Dargo Valley, Queensland, loosely inserted, in the original portfolio of half calf and cloth (rebacked and recornered, each sheet strengthened at inner edge, the foot of the spine nibbled), title lettered in gilt on the front board, Melbourne, Charles Troedel, [1865]. Rare. This was the first album of chromolithographs to have been published in Australia. The album collects together Chevalier’s best Victorian landscapes, most painted during the several tours he undertook through the Victorian wilderness with, among others, Eugen von Guérard and Georg von Neumayer. In this important publication Chevalier and Troedel introduced into Australia the comparatively novel technique of chromolithography – a seminal contribution to the Australian plate book genre, to be followed within months by S.T. Gill’s Australian Sketchbook. His Album of Chromo Lithographs was, to some extent, Chevalier’s final Australian statement: he departed for New Zealand within months and within a year he had won Royal patronage which took him round the world and back to Europe. “Chevalier’s book is the first printed expression of High Victorian taste in landscape art by a key figure in the late romantic era of Australian colonial art. It is furthermore the first major plate book to draw its inspiration from the landscape of Victoria, a landscape that would inspire the greatest works of Australian painting in the remaining decades of the century, ultimately inspiring the seminal works of the Heidelberg School...” (Wantrup). Ferguson, 17329; Kerr, pp. 147-9; Wantrup, 256. Estimate $4000/6000

title: GUÉRARD, Johann Joseph Eugen von.
description: GUÉRARD, Johann Joseph Eugen von. EUGÈNE VON GUÉRARD’S AUSTRALIAN LANDSCAPES. A Series of 24 Tinted Lithographs illustrative of the most striking and picturesque features of the Landscape Scenery of Victoria, New South Wales, South Australia & Tasmania, Drawn from Nature and Lithographed by the Artist, with Letterpress Descriptions of each View… Oblong elephant folio, handcoloured lithographed title-leaf and 24 handcoloured lithographed plates (width circa 485/490 mm), each plate with a single leaf of letterpress description, repairs in the margin plate 14, in the original plum cloth portfolio, lettered in gilt on the front board, rebacked and recornered at an early date in calf. Melbourne, Printed and Published by Hamel & Ferguson, [1867]. Now quite rare: first edition of this famous view book, an important work by colonial Australia’s most accomplished academic artist. This superb collection of High Romantic views of the Australian landscape is based on the most admired oil paintings executed by von Guérard during his first 15 years in Australia, each lithographed by the artist himself. A painstaking artist, noted for his meticulous attention to detail, he also took extraordinary care to ensure that the handcolouring of each plate was properly managed so that there is an appropriate relationship between the original painting and the printed image. “Eugen von Guérard’s Australian Landscapes is the last of the sumptuously produced Australian plate books. By the 1870s the rôle of the topographical plate book was being replaced by the still novel photograph album which offered both a cheaper and a more faithful representation of far-off and familiar places. It is fitting that this last, magnificent finale to the grand plate book tradition should be the work of colonial Australia’s most accomplished academic artist” (Wantrup). Only about 500 copies of Australian Landscapes are said to have been produced, many of which have subsequently been broken up for framing; consequently the complete set is now extremely elusive on the market. Ferguson, 10134a; Kerr, pp. 330-2; Wantrup, 257, Note 1 (q.v.). Estimate $12,000/15,000

title: TROEDEL, Charles (publisher).
description: TROEDEL, Charles (publisher). THE MELBOURNE ALBUM Containing a Series of Views of Melbourne & Country Districts. Respectfully dedicated to, and Patronized by His Excellency Sir Charles Darling, K.C.B. Published by B. Riemann 96, Bourke St., East, Melbourne Opposite Theatre Royal. Price £1.10s. [wrapper title]. Oblong folio, lithographed yellow-ochre titling-wrapper bound in as title-page as issued + 24 fine tinted lithographs, uniform pale stain at upper edge, plates remargined at gutter, one plate on slightly smaller stock and one showing paper thinning at lower corner, two plates with added colour, in publisher’s half red morocco and green cloth sides, the front board lettered in gilt, rebacked with new pastedowns retaining Detmold’s ticket. Melbourne, Charles Troedel, [1863-4]. The complete series and very rare. The set of 24 lithographs that make up Troedel’s Melbourne Album of 1863-4 is the finest work of urban topography produced in Australia in the nineteenth century. Credit for the fine, large and delicately tinted lithographs of scenery in and around Melbourne must go to the publisher who planned and carried through the undertaking, rather than the several artists who worked on it. The Melbourne Album was Troedel’s first venture in publishing. This splendid series of views was issued between August 1863 and July 1864, with the complete series issued in one volume later in 1864 and, more commonly, as ‘short sets’ comprising an ad hoc selection of twelve plates. The lithographs are the work of a number of artists – among them were such notables as Nicholas Chevalier, Eugen von Guérard, and Henry Gritten, but most plates are drawn and lithographed by the little known but highly skilled François Cogné. The complete set is very rare, even the ‘short sets’ are only marginally less rare. Ferguson, 17322; Kerr, pp. 810-11; Wantrup, 262b (“the single most outstanding example of the urban topographical plate book produced in Australia”). Estimate $15,000/20,000

title: TROEDEL, Charles (publisher).
description: TROEDEL, Charles (publisher). THE MELBOURNE ALBUM Containing a Series of Views of Melbourne & Country Districts. Respectfully dedicated to, and Patronized by His Excellency Sir Charles Darling, K.C.B. Published by B. Riemann 96, Bourke St., East, Melbourne Opposite Theatre Royal. Price £1.10s. [wrapper title]. Oblong folio, lithographed pink titling-wrappers as titles + 24 fine handcoloured lithographs, each trimmed and in a window mount, one plate (a few spots of pale foxing) without caption, housed in two modern half morocco bookform boxes. Melbourne, Charles Troedel, [1863-4]. Another complete set, with the lithographs handcoloured. Estimate $12,000/15,000 Voyages and Travels (lots 56 – 89)

title: ARAGO, Jacques Étienne Victor.
description: ARAGO, Jacques Étienne Victor. SOUVENIRS D’UN AVEUGLE… [with final volume:] CHASSES-DRAME… Four volumes, octavo, with 62 lithographed plates, [with] one volume, octavo, with 15 lithographed plates, some plates on toned paper, diffuse foxing, bound with half titles in contemporary French quarter morocco, H.L. White copy with Belltrees bookplate. Paris, Hortet et Ozanne, Éditeurs, 1839 [and] H.L. Delloye, Éditeur, 1840. First edition in a handsome uniform binding. With tipped-in inscribed and signed note by Arago. An extensive rewriting and expansion of Arago’s earlier 1822 narrative of the Freycinet expedition in the Uranie, with numerous illustrations not included in the earlier account, this popular account is effectively a completely new work. The first volume includes a long account of the expedition’s visit to Western Australia, with many illustrations. The third volume is almost entirely devoted to the visit to Hawaii, with many previously unpublished plates – the portraits and depictions of native customs are particularly important. Much of the fourth volume deals with the extended visit of the Uranie to New South Wales, again with many hitherto unpublished plates. Additional scientific notes in this work were contributed by Dominique François Jean Arago. Most sets appear to have a total of 60 plates in the four-volume Souvenirs. Chasses – Drames, the supplementary fifth volume was published in the following year by a different publisher and is quite rare. It comprises a selection of further illustrated reminiscences, many detailing close encounters with wild animals. First work: Bagnall, 124 (undescribed); Davidson, p. 112; Ferguson, 2689a(rev) (but not specifying plates); Forbes, 1134 (calling for 60 plates); Hill 2, 30 (noting 61 plates); Sabin, 1866; Wantrup, 325b (62 plates). Second work: Davidson, p. 112; Ferguson Addenda, 2906aa; not in Forbes; not in Hill (but see note to Hill 2, 30); not in Sabin; Wantrup, 325d. Estimate $1000/2000

title: ARAGO, Jacques Étienne Victor.
description: ARAGO, Jacques Étienne Victor. SOUVENIRS D’UN AVEUGLE. VOYAGE AUTOUR DU MONDE par M. J. Arago, ouvrage enrichi de soixante Dessins et de Notes scientifiques. Four volumes in two, octavo, with 58 lithographed plates (foxed), bound with half-titles in uniform French half burgundy calf and marbled boards of the period, spine decorated in gilt. Paris, Hortet et Ozanne, Éditeurs, 1839. The four-volume first edition of Souvenirs d’un Aveugle, the extensive rewriting and expansion of Arago’s earlier 1822 account of Freycinet’s Uranie expedition. With numerous illustrations not included in the earlier book, it is effectively a completely new work. Originally published in parts between 1838 and 1840, this handsome work was widely popular with many editions and issues. Arago’s Souvenirs has been ill-described in the bibliographies and copies of this first edition have been noted with 58, 60, or 62 plates. Bagnall, 124 (undescribed); Davidson, p. 112; Ferguson Addenda, 2689a(rev) not specifying plates; Forbes, 1134 (calling for 60 plates); Hill 2, 30 (noting 61 plates); Sabin, 1866; Wantrup, 325b (62 plates). Estimate $600/800

title: ARAGO, Jacques Étienne Victor.
description: ARAGO, Jacques Étienne Victor. SOUVENIRS D’UN AVEUGLE... CHASSES. – DRAME. Edition enrichie de 15 dessins. Octavo, with 15 lithographed plates, bound with half-title in French quarter black calf and marbled boards of the period, spine gilt. Paris, H.L. Delloye, Éditeurs, 1840. The rare supplementary volume, Chasses – Drames, was published a year later to complement Arago’s Souvenirs d’un Aveugle. It was published by a different publisher and comprises a selection of further illustrated reminiscences, many detailing close encounters with wild animals. Davidson, p. 112; Ferguson Addenda, 2906aa; not in Forbes; not in Hill; not in Sabin; Wantrup 325d. Estimate $300/500

title: BLIGH, Lieutenant William.
description: BLIGH, Lieutenant William. RÉLATION DE L’ENLÈVEMENT DU NAVIRE LE BOUNTY... avec le Voyage subséquent de cet Officier & d’une partie de son équipage dans sa Chaloupe, depuis les Iles des Amis dans la mer du Sud, jusqu’à Timor, établissement Hollandais aux îles Moluques... Octavo, with three folding maps (some pale staining), with the half-title; bound in old French quarter calf, handsomely decorated in gilt on spine. Paris and Amsterdam, Firmin Didot and Gabriel Dufour, 1790. First French edition of Bligh’s account of the Bounty mutiny. Ferguson, 73. Estimate $500/800

title: BLIGH. WOODARD, David.
description: BLIGH. WOODARD, David. THE NARRATIVE OF CAPTAIN DAVID WOODARD AND FOUR SEAMEN, who lost their ship while in a boat at sea, and surrendered themselves up to the Malays in the Island of Celebes. Octavo, plates (some staining) and two folding maps (with repaired tears), old worn half morocco. London, J. Johnson, 1804. First edition: very scarce. Woodard’s narrative of his shipwreck and capture by the Malays. An appendix includes accounts of other shipwrecks and maritime misadventure, as a warning to mariners, including the Bounty mutiny, the Antelope and Pandora wrecks, and the frightening experiences of the crew of the Shah Hormazier in Torres Strait. Ferguson, 399. Estimate $200/400

title: COOK. HAWKESWORTH, John.
description: COOK. HAWKESWORTH, John. AN ACCOUNT OF THE VOYAGES undertaken by the order of His Present Majesty for making Discoveries in the Southern Hemisphere and successively performed by Commodore Byron, Captain Carteret, Captain Wallis, and Captain Cook... Four volumes, octavo, 2 engraved maps and 9 plates (all folding), minor offsetting, a handsome set in contemporary calf, the spines with contrasting labels. London, W. Strahan and T. Cadell, 1785. First octavo edition and overall third edition of Hawkesworth’s important narrative of James Cook’s voyage in the Endeavour. The octavo edition was more accessible to the general public and had a wider circulation than the expensive quarto editions, despite which it is quite scarce today. Beddie, 665. Estimate $600/800

title: DALRYMPLE, Alexander. VOYAGES DANS LA MER DU SUD PAR LES ESPAGNOLS ET LES HOLLANDOIS. Ouvrage traduit de l’Anglois de M.
description: DALRYMPLE, Alexander. VOYAGES DANS LA MER DU SUD PAR LES ESPAGNOLS ET LES HOLLANDOIS. Ouvrage traduit de l’Anglois de M. Dalrymple, par M. de Fréville. Octavo, with three folding maps, complete with half-title and Privilège leaf, bound in French calf of the period, spine fully gilt (top of the spine with an expert repair), all edges red. Paris, Saillant & Nyon, 1774. First French edition of Dalrymple’s Historical Collection of the Several Voyages and Discoveries in the South Pacific Ocean. The work also includes a translation of Dalrymple’s 1773 very rare Letter from Mr. Dalrymple to Dr. Hawkesworth. The translation and introduction are by Anne François Joachim de Fréville, who translated the official accounts of Cook’s first two voyages and whose important Histoire des Nouvelles Découvertes faites dans la Mer du Sud was published in the same year. Arnot, 26; Davidson, p. 58; Hill 2, 411; Hocken, pp. 8; Sabin, 18344. Estimate $500/800

title: DAMPIER. KNAPTON, James and John (publishers).
description: DAMPIER. KNAPTON, James and John (publishers). A COLLECTION OF VOYAGES. IN FOUR VOLUMES. Containing I. Captain William Dampier’s Voyages round the World… II. The Voyages of Lionel Wafer… III. A Voyage round the World: containing an Account of Capt. Dampier’s Expedition into the South-Seas in the ship St. George... By W. Funnell, Mate to Capt. Dampier. IV. Capt. Cowley’s Voyage round the Globe. V. Capt. Sharp’s Journey over the Isthmus of Darien, and Expedition into the South-Seas. VI. Capt. Wood’s Voyage through the Streights of Magellan. VII. Mr. Roberts’s Adventures and Sufferings amongst the Corsairs of the Levant... Four volumes, octavo, with in total 63 charts and plates, with four pages of terminal advertisements in the first volume, and three in the fourth, an excellent set in speckled calf of the period, joints repaired. London, James and John Knapton, 1729. The collected edition/issue of the voyage accounts published by Dampier’s publisher, James and John Knapton. The main feature – and main selling point at the time – of the set is the complete publication of Dampier’s voyages – initially published in three volumes (the third volume published in two parts) over a ten-year period spanning the end of the seventeenth and the beginning of the eighteenth centuries. The three Dampier volumes are here supplemented by a fourth volume containing complete editions of three related volumes published by the firm: William Funnell’s adverse account of Dampier’s last voyage in the St. George; the account of his buccaneering voyages and travels by Dampier’s associate, doctor turned buccaneer Lionel Wafer; and William Hacke’s edition of the buccaneering voyages of Cowley, Sharp, Wood, and Roberts. Generally regarded as the greatest English explorer and navigator before Cook, Dampier was also a popular and an exciting storyteller who inspired both Swift and Defoe. He was among the first Englishmen to land on the Australian continent in January, 1688. On this occasion Dampier spent some months in New Holland, or Western Australia, living with a group of Aborigines. His thoughtful and objective account of their way of life is the earliest account of any Aborginal Australians. After the huge success of his first volume in 1697, Dampier was given the rank of Captain in the Royal Navy and command of the Roebuck to undertake the first British expedition specifically directed to the exploration of New Holland and the discovery of the east coast. He explored the west coast of New Holland as well as the north coast of New Guinea, discovering New Britain and Dampier Strait. Had his ship not been rotten (and his crew mutinous) he was within a few hundred miles of discovering the east coast of Australia seventy years before Cook when he was forced to turn back. Casey Wood, 309; Clancy, 6.24; Davidson, pp. 32-3; Hill 2, 422; Sabin, 18373. Estimate $6000/9000

title: DUMONT D’URVILLE, J.S.C., and VINCENDON-DUMOULIN, C-A. VOYAGE AU POLE SUD ET DANS L’OCÉANIE sur les corvettes l’Astrolab
description: DUMONT D’URVILLE, J.S.C., and VINCENDON-DUMOULIN, C-A. VOYAGE AU POLE SUD ET DANS L’OCÉANIE sur les corvettes l’Astrolabe et la Zélée, exécuté par ordre du Roi pendant les années 1837-1838-18391840. Histoire. Ten volumes in five, octavo, scattered foxing or browning, pale staining affecting three volumes, modern green cloth, gilt. Paris, Gide, 1841-1846. The complete Histoire section of Dumont D’Urville’s successful second expedition, during which the Astrolabe and Zélée crossed the Antarctic Circle in January 1840 and, taking an unexplored route through the ice, established that there was indeed a land mass. Dumont d’Urville raised the French tricolour at Pointe Géologie, naming that part Adélie Land after his wife. Estimate $1500/3000

title: FLEURIEU, Charles Pierre Claret de.
description: FLEURIEU, Charles Pierre Claret de. DISCOVERIES OF THE FRENCH IN 1768 AND 1769, TO THE SOUTHEAST OF NEW GUINEA, with the subsequent visits to the same lands by English Navigators, who gave them new names. To which is prefixed, an Historical Abridgment of the Voyages and Discoveries of the Spaniards in the same seas. By M. * * *, Formerly a Captain in the French Navy. Translated from the French. Quarto, with 12 folding maps, traces of pale foxing, period calf, rebacked with gilt-decorated spine, some scuffing, the edges of the rear board friable. London, John Stockdale, 1791. The discovery of Mendaña’s lost Solomon Islands. First English edition of this outstanding work of hydrographical detection. Jean François Marie de Surville, on his way south, past New Guinea, New Britain, and New Ireland, literally stumbled on a group of undiscovered islands. He spent some time cruising along the coast, landed his sick there, sought new supplies, and even kidnapped a young native boy. He came into conflict with the inhabitants and so named these islands the Arsacides (“Assassins”) as a warning to others. Although he clearly did not know it at the time, he had discovered the lost islands of Mendaña, the Solomons, that had puzzled geographers for two centuries. Although French hydrographers such as Buache de Neuville had argued the case some years earlier, it was only when the journal of Lieutenant Shortland was published in Governor Phillip’s account of the First Fleet voyage (lot 30) that the French were stirred into public activity. On his return voyage in the Alexander transport from Botany Bay to England, Shortland had passed along a group of islands which he named New Georgia. Fleurieu – a professional naval officer but at this time Minister of Marine under the Revolutionary government – denounced Shortland’s discovery and claimed the honour for de Surville, no proper account of whose voyage had been published. Fleurieu’s exercise in forensic hydrography draws on unpublished manuscript journals as well as the printed narratives of Mendaña, Quirós, Bougainville, Carteret, Cook, Phillip, and others. Writing of the voyage of de Surville, Dunmore remarks that “of far greater importance was the question of the Solomons, which had puzzled geographers since the days of Quirós. Carteret and Bougainville provided the first clues to the answer, but it was de Surville who brought back the conclusive evidence”. Beddie, 1300-3; Davidson, pp. 94-5; Ferguson, 105; Hill 2, 611; Kroepelien, 437; Sabin, 24749; see also Dunmore, I, pp. 135 – 165. Estimate $2400/3000

title: FORREST, Thomas. A VOYAGE TO NEW GUINEA, AND THE MOLUCCAS, and the Moluccas, from Balambangan: including an Account of M
description: FORREST, Thomas. A VOYAGE TO NEW GUINEA, AND THE MOLUCCAS, and the Moluccas, from Balambangan: including an Account of Magindano, Sooloo, and other Islands... performed in the Tartar Galley... during the years 1774, 1775, and 1776… Quarto, 28 (of 31) engraved maps and plates (many folding), several plates oxidised and with strengthening or repairs, modern half calf and marbled boards. London, G. Scott for J. Robson, J. Donaldson, G. Robinson, and J. Bell, 1779. Estimate $200/300

title: FREYCINET. ARAGO, Jacques.
description: FREYCINET. ARAGO, Jacques. VOYAGE AUTOUR DU MONDE SANS LA LETTRE A. Duodecimo, original printed wrappers, in cloth bookform box. Paris, 1853. Rare: only edition. The artist and writer Jacques Arago “certainly had a taste for the facetious and one might even see him as a precursor of the surrealist and dadaist streak in the French creative mind. This last perhaps best seen in a genuinely eccentric book published by him in 1853. A slim duodecimo, Voyage autour du Monde sans la lettre A, endeavours to describe his voyage with Freycinet without using the letter ‘a’. Apart from the title, which a purist might consider a cheat, he successfully brings off this conceit – although decades later he discovered that he had slipped up with one word. This is not, properly speaking, a voyage narrative and hardly essential to a collection but it is a rare and unusual piece worth considering if one aims at completeness. In 2011 Hordern House catalogued a copy … with a long annotation that cleverly avoids using the letter ‘a’ anywhere – a silent cataloguer’s joke that almost certainly flew unnoticed over numerous heads” (Wantrup). See Wantrup, Australian Rare Books 1788-1900, pp. 645-646 (second edition, published this year by Australian Book Auctions). Estimate $500/800

title: HORN, George. ORBIS IMPERANS. Duodecimo, engraved vignette title, early vellum (nicked at one point).
description: HORN, George. ORBIS IMPERANS. Duodecimo, engraved vignette title, early vellum (nicked at one point). Leyden, Lopes de Haro, 1669. Includes reference to Quirós and the East India Company. Estimate $150/300

title: IMAGINARY VOYAGE. BIERVILLAS, Innigo de.
description: IMAGINARY VOYAGE. BIERVILLAS, Innigo de. (pseudonym of Abbé Saunier de Beaumont. VOYAGE D’INNIGO DE BIERVILLAS, PORTUGAIS, À LA CÔTE DE MALABAR, GOA, BATAVIA, & autres lieux des Indes Orientales… Duodecimo, two volumes in one, early inked index on endpaper, stamp on title verso, contemporary mottled calf, spine with small faults at head and foot. Paris, Gregoire-Antoine-Dupuis, 1736. First edition: uncommon. Gove, p. 293; Howgego, B34. Estimate $300/500

title: IMAGINARY VOYAGES. SERIMAN, Zaccaria.
description: IMAGINARY VOYAGES. SERIMAN, Zaccaria. VIAGGI DI ENRICO WANTON ALLE TERRE INCOGNITE AUSTRALI, ed ai regni delle Scimie, e de’ Conicefali nuovamente tradotti da un manoscritto Inglese. Four volumes, plates (many folding), fine copy in pale calf of the period (old worming), spines elaborately gilt in compartments, contrasting spine label. ‘Berna’ [i.e. Venice, Giovanni Battista Remondini], 1764. Rare Italian edition of Seriman’s account of the voyages of the very un-English-sounding English narrator, Enrico Wanton. Shipwrecked on the shores of a South Land, Wanton finds a society of civilised and cultured apes. Coming into favour with them he is soon appointed a minister of state and begins a course of excessive revelry and indulgence, which is depicted in the delightful plates that “show Seriman’s Australia to be very much like a Renaissance Planet of the Apes” (Moors). Davidson, pp. 44-5; Gibson, 769; Gove, p. 314-6; Hill 2, 1553; Hordern House IV, 67; Howgego, S22; Mackaness, 8; Moors, 23 (da Sancha edition); White, p. 142-4, q.v. (edition D). Estimate $1000/2000

title: IMAGINARY VOYAGE. VAIRASSE D’ALLAIS, Denis.
description: IMAGINARY VOYAGE. VAIRASSE D’ALLAIS, Denis. HISTOIRE DES SEVARAMBES, peuples qui habitent une Partie du troisième Continent, communément appellé la Terre Australe. Contenant une Relation du Gouvernement, des Moeurs, de la Religion, & du Langage, de cette Nation, inconnue jusques à present aux Peuples de l’Europe. Two volumes, duodecimo, with frontispieces to each volume (the same plate repeated and so issued) and eight plates; bound without half-titles in speckled calf of the period, spines with raised bands and gilt in compartments, contrasting labels, an attractive copy. Amsterdam, Estienne Roger, 1716. A revised and corrected edition of Estienne’s edition of 1702 with ten new plates. Howgego, V1. Estimate $1000/1500

title: MANGIN, Arthur. VOYAGES ET DÉCOUVERTES OUTRE-MER AU XIXE SIÈCLE. Large octavo, numerous plates, original cloth, decorate
description: MANGIN, Arthur. VOYAGES ET DÉCOUVERTES OUTRE-MER AU XIXE SIÈCLE. Large octavo, numerous plates, original cloth, decorated and gilt, all edges gilt. Tours, A. Mame et Cie, 1880. Originally published in 1863. + BEAUVOIR, Le Comte de. VOYAGE AUTOUR DU MONDE. Tall octavo, very numerous illustrations (many fullpage), quarter morocco of the period, spine elaborately decorated in gilt. Paris, E. Plon, 1878. + ARAGO, Jacques. SOUVENIRS D’UN AVEUGLE. Voyage au tour du Monde. Nouvelle édition revue et augmentée, illustrée de 22 grandes vignettes, portraits et de 150 gravures dans le texte. Octavo, two volumes in one, publisher’s quarter morocco. Paris, H. Lebrun, no date but circa 1843. A new edition. See Ferguson, 3547. Estimate $100/200 Lot 75. An early map of China in Purchas His Pilgrimes

title: MELA, Pomponius. POMPONIUS MELA, TRADUIT EN FRANÇAIS. Three volumes, octavo, two folding engraved maps, a fine set in ea
description: MELA, Pomponius. POMPONIUS MELA, TRADUIT EN FRANÇAIS. Three volumes, octavo, two folding engraved maps, a fine set in early marbled calf, gilt, double spine labels, marbled endpapers and sprinkled edges. Paris, Pougens, 1804. Gronovius’s edition of the Roman geographer Pomponius Mela, one of the main classical works that formed the basis of pre-Renaissance understanding of the world and a key proponent of the Terra Australis incognita myth that led ultimately to the discovery of Australia. Brunet, IV, 801. Estimate $200/300

title: PÉRON, Pierre Francois.
description: PÉRON, Pierre Francois. MEMOIRES DE CAPITAINE PÉRON sur ses voyages aux Cotes d’Afrique, en Arabie, a l’Ile d’Amsterdam, aux Iles d’Anjouan et de Mayotte, aux Cotes Nord-Ouest de l’Amerique, aux Iles Sandwich, à la Chine, etc. Two volumes, octavo, six folding engraved maps and plates, some pale marginal staining in one volume, early quarter morocco, marbled boards. Paris, Brissot-Thivars, 1824. Péron arrived at Sydney on January 23, 1796, on the Ceres, “having been rescued from Amsterdam Island in the South Indian Ocean. The Otter (Boston registry, Capt. Ebenezer Dorr) … arrived on January 24. Dorr offered Péron a position as first officer on his ship to the Northwest Coast and China and return to Boston. While in Sydney, Dorr acquired 18 Botany Bay men as crew, and when the ship left port on February 18, 1796, also smuggled on board was the “Scottish Martyr” Thomas Muir. The Otter in 1796 traded at Nootka Sound and visited Alta California, where many of the Australian crew (and Muir) were left. His was the first American ship to have entered San Francisco Bay. Maps 4 and 5 show the Northwest Coast and the Queen Charlotte Islands” (Forbes). Péron’s accounts of Van Diemen’s Land, Sydney Cove and Botany Bay in 1796 are in Chapter XV. Ferguson, 980; Forbes, 585; Hill, 1330; Sabin, 61001. Estimate $1000/1500 Lot 75. John Smith’s famous map of Virginia

title: PURCHAS, Samuel (circa 1577-1626).
description: PURCHAS, Samuel (circa 1577-1626). HAKLUYTUS POSTHUMUS OR PURCHAS HIS PILGRIMES. Contayning a history of the world, in sea voyages & lande-trauells, by Englishmen & others. Wherein Gods wonders in nature & providence, the actes, arts, varieties & vanities of men, with a world of the worlds rarities, are by a world of eywitnesse-authors, related to the world... In Five Books [engraved title]. Five volumes, folio, with additional engraved title, folding maps (that of Virginia laid down: see illustration above), and with smaller engraved maps, and engraved and woodcut illustrations in the text, with the blank R4 in volume I; a few minor natural flaws and other blemishes (small stains, marginal worming, short tears in some folded maps), an excellent set in early nineteenthcentury calf, back board of third volume detaching (and facing imminent divorce); from the collection of Sir Tom Ramsay with his neat blindstamp. London, Printed by William Stansby for Henrie Fetherstone, 1625-1626. First edition: a handsome set of the massive sequel to Hakluyt. It is, as Sabin remarks in terms echoed by Church, “one of the fullest and most important collections of voyages and travels in the English language”, collecting over 1200 separate narratives of explorations in every part of the world. Many of the accounts relate to the New World, especially Virginia, and one of the engraved maps is Smith’s famous “Map of Virginia”. On his death, Richard Hakluyt left behind a large gathering of original manuscript accounts to which Purchas added many more voyages and travels which he had collected and often translated – Spanish, Portuguse, Dutch, as well as English, among others. These were printed in 1625 as Hakluytus Posthumus, following the general plan of Hakluyt. The first two volumes principally relate to travels in Africa, the Middle East, and Asia; the third volume mainly concerns northern explorations and America; and the fourth volume is almost entirely devoted to America: “accounts of Cortes and Pizarro, Drake, Cavendish, John and Richard Hawkins, Quirós, Magellan, van Noort, Spilbergen, and Barents as well as the categories of Portuguese voyages to the East Indies, Jesuit voyages to China and Japan, East India Company voyages, and the expeditions of the Muscovy Company...” (Hill). The ‘fifth’ volume is the 1626 fourth and best edition of Purchas His Pilgrimage (note the difference in the title). First published in 1613, this separate work was an attempt by Purchas, an Anglican clergyman, to provide a comprehensive account of the world’s religions. It went through three editions before this fourth extended edition was printed as a form of a supplement or addenda to the four volumes of Hakluytus Posthumus. The title-page makes it clear that the ‘fifth’ volume is an integral part of the printed collection. Nevertheless, in very many, if not most, extant sets this volume – unlike in the present set – is a good deal shorter than the four volumes of Hakluytus Posthumus, which suggests at the very least that some contemporary owners saw it as a separate work. Like most early seventeenth-century British books, it was subject to various points of issue or state arising from changes made to the text in the course of printing, as well as alterations made to the many engraved prints and maps as they were printed and reprinted. As usual the engraved title in volume I is in the second state dated 1625 but the text with first issue points (e.g., p. 65 in uncorrected state (with “Hondius His Map of the Christian World”); without the pasted cancellation headlines “English Voyages to the East Indies” on pages 320, 359, 409, etc.; with the first issue headline on page 703-6 “Hollanders lying deuices, to disgrace the English”); Sabin lists other issue points. John Smith’s map of Virginia in volume 4 is in Verner’s state 10 (322 x 410 mm); note that states 7-12 alone were issued with Hakluytus Posthumus and then they are mainly in states 8-10 (state 7 is found only in the very earliest copies gathered, with states 11-12 in the last copies gathered). The last volume, Purchas his Pilgrimage, is the second issue with ‘Purchas’ rather than ‘Purchase’ in the title, and with the added dedication to King Charles. Specific details on request. Borba de Moraes, II, p.692-3; Church, 401A; Hill 2, 1403; Sabin, 66682-6; STC, 20509. Estimate $40,000/60,000

title: ROCHON, Abbé Alexis VOYAGES AUX INDES ORIENTALES ET EN AFRIQUE… Nouvelle Edition.
description: ROCHON, Abbé Alexis VOYAGES AUX INDES ORIENTALES ET EN AFRIQUE… Nouvelle Edition. Octavo, folding map, folding tables, contemporary sprinkled calf (bit dried out on spine). Paris, L’Huillier, 1807. Ferguson, 451. Estimate $300/500

title: SCHOUTEN, Gautier. VOIAGE DE GAUTIER SCHOUTEN AUX INDIES ORIENTALES, Commencé l’An 1658 & fini l’An 1665: Traduit du Hollandois.
description: SCHOUTEN, Gautier. VOIAGE DE GAUTIER SCHOUTEN AUX INDIES ORIENTALES, Commencé l’An 1658 & fini l’An 1665: Traduit du Hollandois. Oú l’on void plusieurs Descriptions de Païs, Roïaumes, Isles & Villes, Siéges, Combats sur terre & sur mer, Coutumes, Maniéres, Réligions de divers Peuples, Animaux, Plantes, Fruits, & autres Curiositez naturelles. Two volumes duodecimo, titles printed in red and black, with frontispieces (both identical, as issued) and nine natural history plates, small collector’s stamp at the bottom of each title-page and on endpapers, bound in mottled calf of the period, spines gilt. Amsterdam, Estienne Roger, 1707. First French edition, following the Dutch edition of 1676 ( a second Dutch edition was published in 1708). A detailed account of Wouter Schouten’s travels in the East Indies between 1658 and 1665. Schouten sailed on the VOC vessel Nieuwpoort in 1658 as assistant surgeon for Batavia. In the course of his travels he visited Amboyna, the Celebes, Bantam, Java, Ceylon, Malacca, and the Coromandel coast as far as the mouth of the Ganges, among others. This edition of Schouten’s voyage was part of René Augustin Constantin de Renneville’s series of French editions of VOC voyages published in Amsterdam by Estienne Roger between 1702 and 1707, under the series title “Receuil des voyages qui ont servir a l’établissement et aux progrès de la Compagnie des Indes Orientales, formé dans les Provinces Unies des Païs-Bas”. Traduit de l’espagnol. Avec une relation de la Guiane de Walter Raleigh, & le Voyage de Narbrough à la Mer du Sud par le Détroit de Magellan, &c. Nouvelle édition... augmentée d’une nouvelle Découverte des Indes Meridionales & Terres Australes, enrichie de figures. Two volumes, duodecimo, eleven engraved plates (many folding) and four folding charts, early calf, rebacked, spines gilt with double labels, marbled endpapers and sprinkled edges. Paris, Denis Horthemels, 1722. The very scarce Paris edition of this account of travel in the New World and the Pacific. The extensive material relating to Australia and the Pacific in volume 2 is translated directly from Robinson’s 1694 Account of Several Late Voyages and Discoveries (new edition 1711), which included Robert Hooke’s translation of the van Nierop edition of Tasman’s journal as well as Narborough’s original journal. In this French version, the Tasman journal is rewritten – inappropriately – in the first person rather than in the third person found in van Nierop and Hooke. This innovation may have been introduced to match the first person narrative of Narborough, which proceeded it, or to add an overall air of authenticity. Needless to say, the ‘Coréal’ of the title-page is apocryphal and no individual undertook all the voyages described. The publisher of the present copy, Denis Horthemels, was one of a conger of Parisian bookseller-publishers who issued it, each with their separate title-page imprints. These five variously issued copies are all different states of the same edition, varying only in the publisher’s imprint on the title-leaf. The Paris edition also has added an attractive folding map, “Hemisphere Meridional Terres Australes”. Centred on the South Pole, it shows the entire Southern Hemisphere including “Terres Australes Nouvelle Hollande” with Tasman’s track and the known coastline of the Australian continent. It is perhaps ironic that this fictitious first-person ‘Coreal’ version of Tasman’s journal was then translated (back) into English by John Barrow and published by him, with some editorial embellishments in 1765 in the second volume of his A Collection of Authentic, Useful, and Entertaining Voyages and Discoveries, Digested in a chronological series (London, J. Only edition of Mathews’s life work, an inestimable contribution to Australasian ornithology, the last of the great colourplate bird books and the most sumptuously produced Australian book of the twentieth century. The edition was limited to 225 numbered copies, of which only a minority are now in private hands. The beautiful handcoloured plates by Keulemans, Gronvold, Green, Goodchild, Frohawk, and others, are also considered the most ornithologically correct and about one hundred species not given in Gould’s Birds of Australia are figured in these volumes. The set is complemented by Mathews’s work on the ornithology of Norfolk and Lord Howe Islands. Although Mathews himself initially insisted that this was to be considered quite a separate publication, he changed his mind with the publication of the final 1936 supplement and it is usually considered a key supplement to the main work, including important additions to the Birds of Australia. In all but the rarest instances, the 1936 Supplement to the Birds of Norfolk and Lord Howe Islands has a substantially reduced number of plates and, for mainly financial reasons, this part was never properly completed or published. Small quarto notebook, bound in stationer’s half calf and marbled boards, somewhat worn and with part of spine lost, the contents detached. Various places, Tasmania, Calcutta, North Shields (Newcastle), circa 1840 to 1865. An uncommon survival, this family commonplace book evidently travelled with Jarbo and his family from one parish to the next. Van Diemen’s Land was then part of the diocese of Calcutta, a geographical oddity that saw considerable cross-fertilisation between India and Van Diemens Land. After service in Van Diemens Land and India, Jarbo was in charge of a parish in North Shields, Newcastle, and was incumbent there when he died in 1865. The commonplace book is in several hands throughout and, while some pieces are signed by Jarbo, others are unsigned and in different hands. Some are dated, some are not. The commonplace book also includes press cuttings and other pasted-in pieces, including a few flyers of a pious nature by Jarbo. What makes this piece of interest are two articles, “Tradition of the Swan River Natives” and “Australia 60 Years Ago”, the first written evidently in the early 1840s (perhaps earlier), the second dated 1848. There are other slight pieces of Australian interest, much of Indian interest, and a loosely inserted letter (dated 1865). Estimate $1000/1500
