New South Wales. Foolscap folio, pp. vi, 126, [2] (endorsement only), first leaf dusty and one opening marked, uncut, modern half calf, gilt. London, Ordered by the House of Commons to be Printed, 30 May 1851. Scarce: relates almost exclusively to assisted emigration to the Port Phillip District prior to the gold rushes. Estimate $200/400

title: PRICE, John. PENAL ESTABLISHMENTS, a Return from the Inspector General [with others].
description: PRICE, John. PENAL ESTABLISHMENTS, a Return from the Inspector General [with others]. Six items, foolscap folio, together in modern binder’s cloth. Melbourne, John Ferres, 1854-1857. A group of six Reports and Annual Reports to the Inspector General, and Reports from the Select Committee, by John Price and others, including Sir Charles Hotham. Estimate $140/240

title: RICKMAN, John. JOURNAL OF CAPTAIN COOK’S LAST VOYAGE TO THE PACIFIC OCEAN, on Discovery; Performed in the Years 1776, 17
description: RICKMAN, John. JOURNAL OF CAPTAIN COOK’S LAST VOYAGE TO THE PACIFIC OCEAN, on Discovery; Performed in the Years 1776, 1777, 1778, 1779... Octavo, five plates (some staining), lacking folding chart, old calf (bit dried out on spine). Dublin, Printed for Messrs. Price, Whitestone, et al., 1781. First Dublin edition. + A copy of the Miegunyah Press’s one volume 2003 edition of Ray Parkin’s H.M. Bark Endeavour, loosely inserted folding plan, original boards with dustwrapper. + A miscellaneous 19th century Cook volume. Estimate $300/500

title: SCHILDER, Gunter. THE SOUTHLAND EXPLORED. The voyage by Willem Hesselsz.
description: SCHILDER, Gunter. THE SOUTHLAND EXPLORED. The voyage by Willem Hesselsz. De Vlamingh in 16961697, with the coastal profiles and a chart of Western Australia in full-size colour reproduction. Elephant folio, plates and maps loose in portfolio as issued, with separate text booklet. Netherlands, 1984. Estimate $100/200

title: SHERER, John. THE GOLD-FINDER OF AUSTRALIA; How He Went, How He Fared, and How He Made His Fortune.
description: SHERER, John. THE GOLD-FINDER OF AUSTRALIA; How He Went, How He Fared, and How He Made His Fortune. Edited by John Sherer. Illustrated with Forty-eight Magnificent Engravings, from authentic sketches taken in the colony. Octavo, pp. xii, 372 + frontispiece (additional pictorial title-page) and 47 other engraved plates, bound in old half calf. London, Clarke, Beeton, &Co., Foreign Booksellers, 148, Fleet Street, [1853]. First edition of this highly popular book, the plates mostly based on S.T. Gill originals – which accounts for their charm – although Sherer acknowledges only the work of the London engraver W.A. Nicholls, merely noting that illustrations are “taken from Drawings made on the spot”. Notoriously, these plates are for the most part reproduced, without permission and without attribution, from Gill’s Sketches of the Victoria Gold Diggings and Diggers As They Are. Ferguson, 15634; Wantrup, 466b. Estimate $300/500

title: SPCK. A VISIT TO AUSTRALIA AND ITS GOLD REGIONS. Octavo, with folding coloured frontispiece map, illustrated with vignet
description: SPCK. A VISIT TO AUSTRALIA AND ITS GOLD REGIONS. Octavo, with folding coloured frontispiece map, illustrated with vignette engravings, original embossed cloth, spine chipped at head and foot. London, Society for the Promotion of Christian Knowledge, 1853. First edition. Ferguson 17982 (noting a variant with inserted advertisements not present in this copy). Estimate $200/300

title: TRAILL, W.H. A QUEENLY COLONY. Pen Sketches and Camera Glimpses.
description: TRAILL, W.H. A QUEENLY COLONY. Pen Sketches and Camera Glimpses. Quarto, numerous black & white illustrations, map, bright original gilt-decorated pebbled cloth. Brisbane, Edmund Gregory, 1901. Estimate $120/240

title: VICTORIA. THOMSON, James (editor).
description: VICTORIA. THOMSON, James (editor). ILLUSTRATED HANDBOOK OF VICTORIA, AUSTRALIA. Colonial and Indian Exhibition, London, 1886. Large octavo, folding map, complete with all engraved plates (some folding), original cloth-backed stiff wrappers. Melbourne, John Ferres, Government Printer, [1866]. Presentation copy from the President and Secretary of the Victorian Royal Commission charged with the conduct of the exhibition. Complete as issued without the plate, “Interior of St Paul’s New Church of England Cathedral”. Ferguson, 8486a. + Cooper’s History of Prahran (1924) in original cloth, Hodder’s biography of George Fife Angas (1891) lacking frontispiece but with a supplied portrait, uncut in original cloth: E. Angas Johnson’s copy, with newspaper cuttings, a photograph, and other related material tipped-in or loosely inserted. Ferguson, 10473 (not calling for a frontispiece), and The Life and Trials of George Barrington, Officer of the Peace at Paramatta, octavo, lacking the portrait, first and final leaves restored, modern sewing, disbound, in folding cloth case. London, Printed by W. Flint by M. Jones, 1803. Estimate $200/300

title: WAHLEN, Auguste. MOEURS, USAGES ET COSTUMES DE TOUS LES PEUPLES DU MONDE. OCEANIE. Octavo, complete with 32 handcoloured
description: WAHLEN, Auguste. MOEURS, USAGES ET COSTUMES DE TOUS LES PEUPLES DU MONDE. OCEANIE. Octavo, complete with 32 handcoloured costume plates, original rubbed quarter calf, head of spine splitting. Brussels, Librairie Historique-Artistique, 1843. The Pacific section of a four-volume work. Estimate $500/700

title: WALCH, Garnet. VICTORIA IN 1880. Quarto, with fine illustrations by Charles Turner, original gilt-decorated cloth over b
description: WALCH, Garnet. VICTORIA IN 1880. Quarto, with fine illustrations by Charles Turner, original gilt-decorated cloth over bevelled boards, gilt edges. Melbourne, George Robertson, [1880]. A popular and attractive work, renowned for its illustrations. Ferguson, 18034. Estimate $300/500

title: WALSH, Grahame L. BRADSHAW ART OF THE KIMBERLEY. Oblong folio, coloured and black & white illustrations, original boards
description: WALSH, Grahame L. BRADSHAW ART OF THE KIMBERLEY. Oblong folio, coloured and black & white illustrations, original boards with pictorial onlay (small abrasion of fore-edge of lower board), with loosely inserted folding prospectus. Toowong, Takarakka Nowan Kas Publications, 2000. Estimate $1200/1500

title: WESTGARTH, William. VICTORIA AND THE AUSTRALIAN GOLD MINES IN 1857; With notes on the Overland Route from Australia, Via Suez.
description: WESTGARTH, William. VICTORIA AND THE AUSTRALIAN GOLD MINES IN 1857; With notes on the Overland Route from Australia, Via Suez. Octavo, handcoloured folding map facing title, two other maps, soiled original cloth. London, Smith, Elder, and Co., 1857. First edition of one of Westgarth’s most important books. The outstanding sociological thinker of his time, he wrote this volume systematically chronicling and analysing the rapid social and economic changes after four years of the gold rush. Ferguson, 18418. + CAPPER, Richard. [An Episode. Batman & Fawkner. Discovery of the River Yarra]. Octavo, lacking wrappers and title, later half morocco. Melbourne, H. Cordell, 1881. Gordon Gidney copy with blindstamps. See Ferguson, 7947. Estimate $200/300

description: WESTGARTH, William. VICTORIA; LATE AUSTRALIA FELIX, or Port Phillip District of New South Wales; being an historical and descriptive account of the Colony and its Gold Mines... Octavo, folding handcoloured map, original salmon cloth, W. R. Griffiths copy with bookplate. Edinburgh, Oliver and Boyd, 1853. First edition. Tipped to the rear board is a 16-page Supplement to the Journal of Commerce of Victoria (May, 1856), folded. Ferguson 18415; Wantrup 449. Estimate $160/220

description: WHITE, John. VOYAGE A LA NOUVELLE GALLES DU SUD, A Botany-Bay, au Port Jackson, en 1787, 1788, 1789. Traduit de l’Anglaise…par Charles Pougens. Octavo, modern half calf retaining earlier boards, David Bremer bookplate. Paris, Pougin, 1795. Ferguson 231 (notoriously calling for plates in error). Estimate $150/300 Literature (lots 227 – 248)

title: BLAKE, William (illustrated by).
description: BLAKE, William (illustrated by). MILTON, John. PARADISE LOST, a Poem in Twelve Books. With a Preface by Peter Ackroyd, and Introduction by John Wain, and Illustrations by William Blake. Quarto, colour plates, quarter morocco, moiré silk boards, slipcase with pictorial onlay. London, The Folio Society, 2003. + A similar Folio Society edition of Dante’s Inferno with Blake’s illustrations (reprinted 2004). Estimate $150/240

title: BRIDGES, Hilda CHINESE LACQUER. An Australian Story.
description: BRIDGES, Hilda CHINESE LACQUER. An Australian Story. Octavo, original blue cloth lettered and decorated in black. London, Hodder and Stoughton, [1926]. First edition: scarce Australian novel: signed by the author. Estimate $120/240

title: DE GOY, André AVENTURES SUR MER ET SUR TERRE, I. La Famille Laurencay.
description: DE GOY, André AVENTURES SUR MER ET SUR TERRE, I. La Famille Laurencay. II. Histoire d’un Jeune Chercheur d’Or en Australie. Octavo, plates, scattered foxing, original gilt-decorated cloth, edges gilt. Paris, Alphonse Desesserts, [1852]. Includes “probably the first account of the Australian goldfields in fiction” (O’Neill). O’Neill, 103. Estimate $300/500

description: DEVANNY, Jean. SUGAR HEAVEN. edition, scarce cloth issue. Estimate $100/200 Octavo, original coffee cloth. Sydney, Modern Publishers, 1936. First

description: FOLIO SOCIETY. The Brontes. SEVEN NOVELS. Agnes Grey; The Tenant of Wildfell Hall; Jane Eyre; The Professor; Shirley; Villette; and Wuthering Heights. Seven volumes, octavo, illustrations, original decorated leatherbacked cloth in slipcases. London, Folio Society, 1964-70. Complete set. Estimate $80/120

title: GARD, Roger Martin du.
description: GARD, Roger Martin du. LES THIBAULT... Lithographies originales de Berthold Mahn. Eight volumes, octavo, illustrated, half morocco, marbled boards, top edge gilt. Paris, Imprimerie Nationale, Andre Sauret, 1960. Attractive limited edition of 3000 numbered sets. + THÉATRE CLASSIQUE FRANÇAIS. Twelve volumes, octavo, leatherbound. Paris, Les Editions du Cap, 1959. Limited edition of 1852 numbered sets. Estimate $100/200

title: GREENAWAY, Kate. ALMANACK FOR 1883 [and following years].
description: GREENAWAY, Kate. ALMANACK FOR 1883 [and following years]. Twenty-two volumes, including six duplicates in variant bindings, duodecimo and oblong duodecimo, each colour illustrated throughout, various publisher’s bindings of wrappers, glazed boards, cloth, semi-limp morocco, very good to fine copies. London, Routledge, Dent or Warne, also Paris, Hachette, 1882-1894, 1896, 1923-1924. First editions, a continuous run from Almanack for 1883 to Almanac for 1897 (no issue was published in 1896), also with the issues for 1924 and 1925. Included in the lot are two copies of Greenaway’s Birthday Book for Children (one inscribed in 1885), Queen Victoria’s Jubilee Garland (1887, wrappers, the ribbon tie replaced), Kate Greenaway’s Alphabet, and a group of 16 attractive Christmas cards, Valentine cards, and Merit Reward cards, coloured and gilt. Estimate $1400/1800

title: McCUAIG, Ronald. VAUDEVILLE. Tall octavo, original green cloth, marked and spotted (as usual), entirely uncut, as issued without dustwrapper.
description: McCUAIG, Ronald. VAUDEVILLE. Tall octavo, original green cloth, marked and spotted (as usual), entirely uncut, as issued without dustwrapper. Potts Point (Sydney), Privately Printed by The Author, 1938. Rare: edition of 150 numbered and signed copies. + A good group of Australian Literature. Estimate $120/180

description: SCHOLARTIS PRESS. MACKENZIE, Henry. THE MAN OF FEELING. Octavo, edges uncut, original clothbacked boards with dustwrapper. London, Scholartis Press, 1928. Edition limited to 1475 copies. + Four other works from the same press. Estimate $80/120

description: STEAD, Christina. THE SALZBURG TALES. Octavo, original salmon pink cloth (bit sunned on spine), with custom made navy morocco backed book-form box. London, Peter Davies, 1934. First edition: signed by the author. Estimate $200/400

description: STEAD, Christina. THE MAN WHO LOVED CHILDREN.
